definition: AI systems that process and combine more than one kind of input or output, such as text, images, audio and video.
details: Multimodal models align different modalities into shared representations so they can caption an image, answer questions about a chart, or generate a video from text. They underpin modern assistants that see, hear and read at once.

explainer.lead: Multimodal AI processes and combines more than one kind of input or output, such as text, images, audio and video. It matters because assistants can now see, hear and read at once.

tiers.eli5: Like a friend who can look at a picture, listen to a recording and read a note, then answer questions using all three.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers align different modalities into shared representations so one model can caption images, answer questions about charts or generate video from text. A pitfall is that weak alignment between modalities degrades performance on cross-modal tasks.
tiers.paperLevel: Systems align multiple modalities into shared representations, enabling tasks such as image captioning, chart question answering and text-to-video generation. Limits: cross-modal alignment and data coverage vary by modality pair.

explainer.example: A user uploads a photo and asks a spoken question; the assistant reads the image, hears the question and replies in text.

citation.title: Multimodal Machine Learning: A Survey and Taxonomy
citation.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 41(2)
